cyberimplants.manual.title: Field Manual
cyberimplants.manual.start.title: First steps
cyberimplants.manual.start.body:
# What is this mod?
Create: Cybernetics lets you replace parts of your body with implants. You build them on Create production lines, install them in a kinetic surgical chair, and teach them tricks with a programmable cyberdeck.

# The whole road in 8 steps
- 1. Craft a Cybernetic Core (Mechanical Crafter). Nothing else works without it.
- 2. Craft an Implantation Rig and a Kinetic Charger, and power both with a shaft.
- 3. Make Bio-Interface Gel in a Mechanical Mixer and put it into the Rig.
- 4. Craft some Tier I implants (see the recipes in JEI / the recipe book).
- 5. Right-click the Rig, install the Core first, then everything else.
- 6. Keep an eye on Neural Load and Charge (chapters 2 and 3).
- 7. Hold {key:wheel} to use your implants.
- 8. Upgrade implants to higher tiers with sequenced assembly (chapter 6).

> You can open this manual any time with {key:manual}, or by right-clicking the Field Manual item. It remembers the page you stopped on.

# Recipe book
Every implant has a recipe: Tier I is crafted, Tiers II to V are upgrades of the previous tier. Look an implant up in JEI or the recipe book; hover an implant to see its tier, Neural Load and what it unlocks.

! This mod is still under development. Some features listed in item tooltips are not finished yet.
cyberimplants.manual.body.title: Body, Core and Load
cyberimplants.manual.body.body:
# Regions and slots
Your body has regions, and every region accepts one category of implant:
- Core (1): Cybernetic Core. Mandatory, install it first.
- Cortex (2): Neural Systems.
- Spine (1): Cyberdeck chassis. Deck modules go into the chassis sockets.
- Ocular (2): Optical implants.
- Skeleton (3): Skeletal and muscular.
- Left / Right Arm (1 each): Cybernetic Arm. Limb modules go into the arm's sockets.
- Circulatory (3), Integument (2), Legs (2).
You cannot install two of the same implant in one region (arm modules may be in both arms).

# Neural Capacity and Load
Every implant has a Neural Load shown in its tooltip. Your Core has Neural Capacity: 30 / 45 / 60 / 80 / 100 for Tiers I to V.
- Load up to Capacity: Stable.
- Load a little above Capacity (the Core's overload margin): Strained. Every minute or two a glitch knocks one active implant offline for 3 to 5 seconds, and all Charge costs are +20%.
- Load above that: the Rig refuses to install the implant.
Upgrading the Core is the main way to fit more hardware.

# Neuro-Stabilizer
A bottle that suppresses glitches for 10 minutes (you feel sick for the first 5 seconds). Make it by spouting a Glass Bottle with 250 mB of Neural Gel.

# Death
Your implants stay in your body when you die. You respawn with 25% Charge.

> Host tier limits child tier: an arm module cannot be a higher tier than the arm, and a deck module cannot be a higher tier than the chassis.
cyberimplants.manual.charge.title: Charge (energy)
cyberimplants.manual.charge.body:
# What is Charge?
Charge is the battery of your Core. Active implants spend it when used, toggled implants spend it every second, and some passive ones cost nothing. The bar is shown near the hotbar.

# Battery size
Core Tier I to V: 100 / 200 / 350 / 500 / 750 Charge.

# Where Charge comes from
- Your body converts food into Charge slowly (about 0.25 to 1 per second, better Cores are faster). It stops when you are hungry, so eat.
- Kinetic Charger: stand on the pad. It gives |RPM| / 8 Charge per second (32 per second at 256 RPM) and needs at least 16 RPM.

# When you run out
An implant that needs Charge you do not have simply fails: nothing is spent and no cooldown starts.

> Server owners can switch the energy system off in the server config (charge.enabled). Then everything is free, but cooldowns are 1.5 times longer.

! A Strained body (Load above Capacity) pays 20% more for everything.
cyberimplants.manual.rig.title: Implantation Rig
cyberimplants.manual.rig.body:
# Building it
- Implantation Rig: iron sheets, a Precision Mechanism, an Andesite Casing, a shaft and a cogwheel. It is a surgical stool: the shaft goes into the gearbox at its back.
- Connect a shaft to it. The Rig needs rotation to work.
- Bio-Interface Gel: Mechanical Mixer (no heat), 250 mB water + slime ball + bone meal + sugar.
- Neural Gel (for Tier IV and V): heated Mixer, 250 mB Bio-Interface Gel + lapis + glowstone dust + amethyst shard.
- Fill the Rig's tank (1000 mB) with a bucket or a pipe.

# Requirements by implant tier
|Tier I / II / III / IV / V
|Time:  5 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 20 seconds
|Speed: 16 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 RPM
|Gel:   250 mB (Bio-Interface for I to III, Neural for IV and V)

# The screen
- Right-click the Rig. Left: the implants in your inventory. Centre: a hologram of your skeleton with a node on every body slot. Right: details of whatever you point at.
- The top bar shows the Rig's speed and gel, and your Neural Load. With an implant selected, a ghost segment shows the Load it would add.
- Pick an implant: the slots it fits glow green. Click one to start. Double-clicking an implant installs it in the first slot that fits.
- Click an installed node to inspect it, then Extract (click twice to confirm). Drag the hologram to turn it.
- The details panel plays a preview of the implant's effect and lists its stats, compared with the one you have installed or with the next tier, its features and what the operation needs (a red cross marks what is missing).

# The operation
- When the operation starts the Rig straps you onto its stool: you cannot walk, jump or stand up until it finishes. The screen and the top of your HUD show the progress.
- Install the Core first. Removed implants return to your inventory with their tier.

! The operation aborts if the Rig slows below the needed RPM, runs out of gel, or you leave the chair some other way (an ender pearl, for instance). You take 4 damage and the implant stays where it was.

> A redstone signal on the Rig locks it (useful for a clinic door). A comparator reads the operation progress.
cyberimplants.manual.controls.title: Controls
cyberimplants.manual.controls.body:
# Keys (all rebindable)
- Hold {key:wheel}: the Implant Wheel. Point at an implant and release to use it or toggle it.
- {key:dodge}: dodge (needs Kerenzikov).
- {key:fire_ballistic}: fire the Ballistic Module.
- {key:deck}: open the cyberdeck editor.
- {key:manual}: open this manual.
- Deck Macro Keys 1 to 4 are unbound until you assign them in the controls menu.

# How implants are used
- Passive: always working, nothing to do.
- Toggle: switch on and off in the wheel (costs Charge every second while on).
- Active: use from the wheel; has a Charge cost and a cooldown.
- Input-bound: uses normal keys (see below).
- Triggered: fires by itself when its condition happens.

# Movement implants
- Enhanced Tendons: press Jump again in the air.
- Hydraulic Legs: hold Sneak, hold Jump, release to leap where you look.
- Microgrip: hold Sneak against a wall to cling and climb.
- Magnetic Soles: toggle on, then walk up metal walls.
- Momentum Booster: sprinting fills a gauge; use it from the wheel to dash.

# Combat implants
- Sandevistan: creates a slow-time field around the spot where you stand.
- Retractable Blade: toggle on; strikes with an empty hand.
- Remote Manipulator: use buttons, levers and doors from a distance.
- Optical Camouflage and Target Tracking: from the wheel.

> The wheel only lists Active and Toggle implants. Cooldowns start when the effect ends.
cyberimplants.manual.tiers.title: Tiers and upgrades
cyberimplants.manual.tiers.body:
# Five tiers
I Civilian, II Industrial, III Advanced, IV Military, V Experimental. There is one item per implant; its tier is shown as Mk. I to V in the name and tooltip.

# How to get a higher tier
Tier I implants are crafted. Every higher tier is an upgrade: put the implant of the previous tier into a Create sequenced assembly (deployer, spout, press, and so on, repeated several times). The previous implant is consumed. You cannot skip tiers.
- Tier II: for example brass sheets, electron tubes and Bio-Interface Gel, one loop.
- Tier III to V: more loops and rarer parts. Tier V uses Neural Gel, Echo Shards and Netherite.

# What a tier changes
- Numbers: radius, duration, cooldown, damage, range, charges.
- Unlocks: new abilities that appear at certain tiers. The tooltip shows what is unlocked at this tier.
- The Rig needs more RPM, time and the better gel.

> Your settings stay with you when you swap or upgrade an implant.

! Higher tiers cost more Neural Load. Check Capacity before you upgrade.
cyberimplants.manual.catalog.title: Implant catalog
cyberimplants.manual.catalog.body:
# Neural Systems (Cortex, 2)
- Sandevistan: slows everything inside a temporal field.
- Reflex Booster: faster attacks, bow draw, eating.
- Combat Predictor: lead marker for ranged weapons.
- Automatic Evasion System: sidesteps arrows.
- Kerenzikov: dodge key and a reaction window.

# Cyberdecks (Spine and deck sockets)
Chassis, Processor, RAM, Storage, Coprocessor, Machine Interface. See chapter 8.

# Skeletal and Muscular (Skeleton, 3)
Reinforced Skeleton, Power Actuators, Kinetic Tendons (jump), Micro-Actuators (sprint), Impact Dampeners (falls), Inertia Compensation (knockback).

# Limbs (Arms)
Cybernetic Arm (frame), Retractable Blade, Remote Manipulator, Microgrip, Ballistic Module (flechettes).

# Optical (Ocular, 2)
Entity Scanner, Thermal Vision, Machine Analyzer, Ballistic Visor, Optical Camouflage, Target Tracking.

# Circulatory (3)
Biomonitor, Regenerator, Adrenaline Pump, Emergency Defibrillator, Energy Buffer, Emergency Response System.

# Subdermal (Integument, 2)
Armor Plating, Nanocoating, Shock Circuit, Kinetic Shield, Emergency Shell.

# Mobility (Legs, 2)
Enhanced Tendons, Hydraulic Legs, Silent Actuators, Magnetic Soles, Inertial Stabilizer, Momentum Booster.

> Slots are fewer than implants, so you must choose. That is the point of the mod.
cyberimplants.manual.deck_build.title: Building a cyberdeck
cyberimplants.manual.deck_build.body:
# What it is
A cyberdeck is a tiny computer in your spine. It runs programs written in Synapse that watch your senses and fire your implants for you.

# Parts
A deck needs all of these, installed in the Rig:
- Cyberdeck Chassis in the Spine slot. It has module sockets (3 at Tier I).
- Processor: runs the program. Tier decides how fast it is and which language level (ISA-1 to ISA-5) it understands.
- RAM: memory for the running program.
- Storage: where your programs are saved.
Install the modules into the deck sockets. Each costs 1 extra Neural Load.

# Optional parts
- Coprocessor: one more program at the same time.
- Machine Interface: more Neural Ports and longer range (chapter 11).

! Without a chassis, Processor, RAM and Storage the deck does not boot. The editor will tell you what is missing.

> A module cannot be a higher tier than its chassis.
cyberimplants.manual.synapse.title: Your first program
cyberimplants.manual.synapse.body:
# Opening the editor
Press {key:deck}. The Programs tab has a list on the left and an editor on the right. The Processes tab shows what is running, the Log tab shows messages and errors.

# Saving and running
- Write your program, press Save. Errors are shown with the line number.
- Press Load to start it. Unload stops it.
- ON boot runs when the program is loaded.

# Example 1: automatic slow-motion
Fires the Sandevistan when something dangerous is near.
|PROGRAM "Chrono Guard"
|REQUIRES entity_scanner, sandevistan
|
|ON enemy_detected:
|    IF distance < 8:
|        ACTIVATE sandevistan

# Example 2: a key of your own
Assign Deck Macro Key 1 and 2 in the controls menu first.
|PROGRAM "Macro"
|ON key 1:
|    ACTIVATE sandevistan
|ON key 2:
|    TOGGLE thermal

# Example 3: panic button
Needs a Biomonitor to measure health.
|PROGRAM "Panic Button"
|ON health_below 8:
|    ALERT "Low health!"
|    ACTIVATE camo

# Example 4: scan every ten seconds
Needs Processor Tier II (ISA-2) for EVERY.
|PROGRAM "Scout"
|EVERY 10s:
|    SCAN

> A script pays exactly what you would pay by hand: the same Charge, cooldown and range.
cyberimplants.manual.synapse_ref.title: Synapse cheat sheet
cyberimplants.manual.synapse_ref.body:
# Rules
- Everything lives inside handlers. A line ending with : opens a block; indent the lines inside it.
- Comments start with #. Keywords are not case-sensitive.
- Durations: 20t, 500ms, 3s, 2m.

# Handlers
- ON boot: when the program starts.
- ON enemy_detected: Entity Scanner found something (distance, kind, entity).
- ON damaged: needs a Biomonitor (amount, family, attacker).
- ON health_below 8: needs a Biomonitor.
- ON charge_below 50: low Charge.
- ON dodge, ON key 1, ON strain_changed, ON landed and more.
- EVERY 5s: timer (ISA-2).
- ON rotational_speed_changed FROM press: a bound machine port.

# Statements
- LET x = 5, SET x = x + 1, VAR n = 0 (program-wide)
- IF / ELIF / ELSE
- ACTIVATE name, DEACTIVATE name, TOGGLE name
- LOG "text", ALERT "text"
- SCAN
- STOP: unload the program
- ISA-2: WHILE, REPEAT 3 TIMES, BREAK, CONTINUE, WAIT 1s, SEND redstone_signal TO port STRENGTH 15

# Reading yourself
self.charge, self.charge_max, self.load, self.capacity, self.position, self.on_ground, self.sprinting

# Implant names
sandevistan, reflex, aes, kerenzikov, scanner, thermal, camo, tracker, bio, regen, adrenaline, defib, shield, shell, soles, momentum, hydraulics, air_jump, ballistic, blade, manipulator and more.

> A task that runs too long without WAIT is killed by the watchdog. The program keeps running.

! You can only use implants you really have installed.
cyberimplants.manual.machines.title: Machines (Create)
cyberimplants.manual.machines.body:
# Neural Port
A small plug that exposes a machine to your deck.
- Place it on a side of a Create machine.
- To give it a name, rename the item in an anvil before placing.
- Right-click your own port to bind it to your deck. Right-click again to unbind.
- A Tier I deck binds 2 ports within 16 blocks. A Machine Interface raises both numbers.

# Reading a machine
|PROGRAM "Overspeed Guard"
|DEVICE press = port "Press Line A"
|
|ON rotational_speed_changed FROM press:
|    IF ABS(rotational_speed) > 128:
|        ALERT "Press Line A is too fast"
Available: press.speed, press.abs_speed, press.online.

# Controlling a machine
A Neural Port can also output redstone (Machine Interface Tier II, ISA-2). Use it for clutches, gearshifts, lamps.
|PROGRAM "Warden"
|DEVICE press = port "Press Line A"
|DEVICE lamp = port "Alarm Lamp"
|
|ON rotational_speed_changed FROM press:
|    IF ABS(rotational_speed) > 128:
|        SEND redstone_signal TO lamp STRENGTH 15
|    ELSE:
|        SEND redstone_signal TO lamp STRENGTH 0

# Other blocks
- Kinetic Charger: charges you (chapter 3).
- Proximity Sensor: detects creatures in a box and outputs a redstone signal.
- Machine Analyzer implant: works like Engineer's Goggles without a helmet.

> The deck itself is limited by its range; a Neural Port further away than the Machine Interface range goes offline.
cyberimplants.manual.tips.title: Tips and troubleshooting
cyberimplants.manual.tips.body:
# Nothing happens in the Rig
- "Needs rotation": connect a shaft and spin it. Check the RPM for your implant tier.
- "Needs X mB of gel": fill the tank. Tier IV and V need Neural Gel.
- "Install a Cybernetic Core first": the Core goes in before anything else.
- "Its tier is higher than its host": upgrade the arm or chassis first.
- "Neural Load too high": upgrade the Core or remove something.

# My implant does not work
- "Not enough Charge": stand on a Kinetic Charger.
- "Not ready": cooldown. It starts when the effect ends.
- "Offline (neural glitch)": you are Strained. Use a Neuro-Stabilizer or lower your Load.
- "No target in sight" or "Out of range": aim at something.
- Is it installed? Active implants are in the wheel only if installed.

# My program does not run
- Check the Log tab. The deck needs a chassis, Processor, RAM and Storage.
- ISA-1 does not have WAIT, EVERY or loops. Upgrade the Processor.
- Programs need the implants they use, or they will not load.

# Good habits
- Build the Kinetic Charger near the Rig and your base.
- Keep a spare Neuro-Stabilizer for big fights.
- Save good programs: Storage keeps them, so you can load them again later.
- Do not install a Tier V implant you cannot power: the Rig needs 256 RPM.

> Keys are in Options, Controls. Server rules (such as the first-join manual or Charge) are in the server config.
